svg.text: From Composer source to a tested native operation, then to a portable microservice project
Follow stages 1–9. Component-level validation and operation-level validation are separate checkpoints.
XML operation, format and step definitions
Selected operations are the conversion roots
Parse Java and Composer XML relationships
Generate a map or verify an existing map
Retain source fingerprints and reusable analysis
Collect formats, OpSteps, classes and operations
Select reusable JARs or registered HTTP APIs
AI converts missing base formats and OpSteps
Preserve typed APIs and configuration behavior
Compile and run AI-generated JUnit tests
Mock external services, databases and resources
Compare XML format behavior with shared fixtures
Compose accepted formats and operation steps
Recreate routing, data flow and error handling
Generate HTTP clients for called operations
Execute JUnit tests for operation behavior/routes
Use mocks for external systems and called APIs
Retain validated XML samples and test evidence
Wrap accepted business code with a REST API
Configure service addresses and runtime settings
Build/test the JAR; validate Helm output
Keep Java/Maven sources, tests and shared JARs
Include launchers, config, Helm and documentation
Develop and maintain the delivered project
Compatible converted code can skip another AI conversion. Current-source, API and build/test checks still apply.
SQLite checkpoints every stage. Failures return diagnostics to the relevant implementation or test work.
Deliverables include standalone and microservice outputs; the portable project retains the source and tests needed for maintenance.
Mocks replace external dependencies in tests, not the business behavior being validated. Format comparisons use observed XML cases.
Source/AST analysis stays enabled. Formal fact collection/validation stays disabled. Image publication and deployment are user actions.
